newsitem.title: UK: NSea crude looks to storage to bolster weak market.
newsitem.headline: NSea crude looks to storage to bolster weak market.

text.p: North Sea markets were quiet and steady on Wednesday with dealers hoping the steep price contango will push barrels into storage and relieve the overhang of June barrels.

With most players reading the American Petroleum Institute (API) stock data as broadly neutral, market talk was balanced between those expecting weaker differentials and those thinking Brent had hit bottom.
No wet Brent deals were seen early Wednesday but offers were believed to be around July -70 cents, the level of yesterday's trade.
"Its all a bit slow out there," said one trader. "There was a bit of a build on distillates and gasoline in the APIs so there was not much for the bulls in the figures.
"I think what the market is looking at now is the extent of the contango and whether it will cover the cost of storage."

July/August spreads lost one cent to trade on Wednesday at -32 cents, very close to the 35 cent gap one trader estimated necessary to cover the expense of tanking the surplus of June barrels dragging down the market.
"Storage will not make the market stronger but it will put a floor under it," said one player.
"There are still a lot of June grades, including Brent, not yet committed, with no end-users buying and refiners already covered," said another trader. "Most probably premiums will drop again."
Some sellers were hopeful that better refinery margins in the wake of Brent's $3 drop in the last three weeks will persuade operators to run flat-out and help soak up supply.
In late trades on Monday a 24-26 June loading Oseberg was heard done at dated Brent -10 cents, 5 cents weaker than earlier that day. Two late June loading Ekofisk cargoes traded at dated even.
Outright July paper traded at $17.64, a mild recovery from year-lows on the screen hit late on Tuesday night in thin trade.
Short-dated swaps weakened for the front week but recovered further out. Contracts for differences for the week June 16-20 against July were bid at -42 cents and offered at -32 cents.
